title: Two-time interval method to circumvent particle image velocimetry dynamic range
author: Bharadwaj, Vybhav

steps.title: Set laser pulse intervals
steps.instruction: Configure the dual‑laser head so that the time interval between the two laser pulses (Δt) can be as low as a few micro‑seconds; set a short interval Δt1 = 1 ms and a long interval Δt2 = 100 ms (Δt2 > Δt1). Ensure the laser operates at a frequency between 10 Hz and a few kHz.

steps.title: Capture image sequence
steps.instruction: Synchronise the PIV camera with the laser and run a single acquisition that records three images (1, 2, 3) according to the timing diagram: images 1–2 are separated by Δt1 and images 1–3 by Δt2.

steps.title: Compute PIV vectors
steps.instruction: Using PIV software, calculate the velocity vector field for each image pair (1‑2 and 1‑3). Each instant of the flow field yields an M × N array of vectors.

steps.title: Apply normalized median test
steps.instruction:
Select a window size of 3 × 3 or 5 × 5 (n = (window size)²). For every vector cell:
1. Compute the median of the vectors in the window: Um = Median(U1, U2, …, Un).
2. Calculate residuals for each vector i in the window: ri = |Ui − Um|.
3. Determine the median residual: rm = Median(ri).
4. Normalise the median residual: r′ = rm / Um.
Use the normalised median residual r′ to identify and flag spurious vectors.
